witness.comment: The OpenITI primary version of Ibn Hisham's Sira: the release metadata of OpenITI 2025.1.9 lists it with status 'pri', 278,907 tokens and 1,090,736 characters (OpenITI's counts), tagged PRIMARY_VERSION, CLEANED_VERSION and COMPLETED. Its version metadata names Mathew Barber as annotator and records that footnote markers and paratext were removed in the OpenITI clean operation of 2023, and a collation against http://www.worldcat.org/oclc/295009190. The file's own header gives the author's death as 213 AH (OpenITI's author record: '0213-XXX-XX or 0218-RA2-13'). Five other OpenITI versions of the same book exist (JK000797, Masaha003361Vols, ShamAY0034440, Shamela0007450, Shia003667Vols); none was used.

work.label: The Sira of Ibn Ishaq (the work itself, known through its recensions)
work.comment: Ibn Ishaq's biography of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) as an abstract work (docs/02 §8.9). It survives here through Ibn Hisham's recension, which also contains Ibn Hisham's own additions, each marked in the text by 'qala Ibn Hisham'.

recension.label: Ibn Hisham's recension: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya
recension.comment: The source chosen by the maintainer (decision E32). The Arabic title is the one in the OpenITI file's metadata (020.BookTITLE). OpenITI's URI dates the author 213 AH; the author's death is also given as 218 AH (OpenITI author record: '0213-XXX-XX or 0218-RA2-13'). Which is right is not decided here.

edition.label: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya li-Ibn Hisham, ed. Mustafa al-Saqqa, Ibrahim al-Abyari and Abd al-Hafiz Shalabi, 2nd edition, 1375 AH / 1955 CE (PROVISIONAL)

edition.comment: PROVISIONAL (maintainer decision E33: the scholars will specify the edition of record). This is the base edition the OpenITI file names in its metadata (040.EdEDITOR, 041.EdNUMBER and 043.EdPUBLISHER, quoted in dct:bibliographicCitation, the three fields joined by semicolons). Volume and page numbers cited in this corpus are this edition's as the OpenITI file marks them (PageV01P158 = vol. 1, p. 158; OpenITI puts each marker at the end of its page). They have not been checked against a printed copy.

agent_comment: A generic software agent: the AI-assisted extraction pass of slice 4, run on 15 October 2026, which read passages of Ibn Hisham's Sira in the OpenITI text and proposed reports, chains and claims with their exact spans. Every claim it made is proposed and unreviewed; its English glosses are machine-written and are not translations. Which system ran the pass is deliberately not recorded in the repository.
